title: Show Me Again
can_do: 听不懂一个指令时直接说明，并请求一次示范。
trigger: Rabbit Teacher gives a clap-then-tap pattern; Child does not understand the order and asks to see it once before trying.
setting: A short hands-and-knees movement game in a quiet school corner.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.line: New game. Clap your hands, then tap your knees.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: I don't understand. Can you show me?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: First clap, then tap. Like that?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Clap... and tap. I understand now!

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Clap and tap! This game is fun.

replay_cards.title: Show me beside
replay_cards.change: Teacher asks Child to place a card beside the box, but Child is unsure of the location
replay_cards.challenge: Child says it is unclear and asks to see an example. Teacher places a separate card beside the box. Child checks the location by pointing, then puts his own card beside the box and confirms that he understands.

replay_cards.title: Show me fold
replay_cards.change: Dad asks for a napkin folded in half, but Child does not know which edges to bring together
replay_cards.challenge: Child says, 'I don't understand. Can you show me?' Dad slowly folds his own napkin once. Child points to the matching edges of his second napkin to check, folds it himself, and places it beside Dad's.

parent_support: Treat not understanding as useful information. A brief puzzled look and an ordinary request are enough; do not demand guessing or an apology.
After he asks, show one slow, visible clap followed by one gentle tap on your own knees. Keep your voice normal and your hands in view.
Answer his order check, then let him perform the pattern. Do not move his hands, clap over him, add props, or turn success into theatrical praise.
